title: [CQ-V12] Delivery integration and hardening
description:
Objective: Exercise trusted dispatch, review, admission, crashes, dependencies and architecture end to end.

Deliverable: Delivery integration and hardening. This is task V12 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): V09, V11.
definitionOfDone: All dependency projections agree with QA and delivery.
Whole epic docs and adversarial diff review complete with fresh regression evidence.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY ONCE: the epic-final gate.

The epic touched shared schema, wire and launcher surfaces, so this is FULL regression across every package it touched. Run it fresh in an isolated Linux snapshot (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate):
- a `git archive` of the WHOLE repo at HEAD, with only this task's doc edits overlaid;
- `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` per package, after checking that each lockfile matches its tree modulo CR;
- `env -i` with HOME, NO_COLOR=1 and a Linux-only PATH, so no MOE_* variable is set.
Never run moe-proxy's npm test in the shared tree: its pretest cleans and rebuilds dist/.

1. `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` must exit 0. Supply its command, exit code and output tail to complete_task (DoD 4).
2. Also run these, and report each with its pass/skip numbers in the completion summary:
   - `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit`.
   - `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/__acceptance__`: the V11, V12a and V12b acceptance files must pass UNCHANGED. Run `git log --oneline -- packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__`. Any edit after a file's owning task landed is a finding for step 5.
   - `cd packages/moe-proxy && npm test`, in the snapshot only.
   - `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, which includes V07's intent-*, V08's reconcile-strong-* and V08b's modes. Widen MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC on a busy box.
   - postflight.ps1 under pwsh, and under Windows PowerShell 5.1 when reachable. If an engine is unavailable, say so; never claim it ran.
   - `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`.
   - `node --test scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs scripts/tests/agent-runtime.test.mjs scripts/tests/resume-progress.test.mjs`.
   - `npm run lint` at the repo root.
3. Diagnose a red run; never retry it into green. Re-run a known load-sensitive timing test (for example waitForTask.test.ts) alone, and report both runs. A real failure in code this plan does not own becomes a step-5 finding.

comments.author: qa-7c627d35
comments.content:
QA hand-forward from CQ-V01 (approved 2026-10-26). Two test gaps, non-blocking, for this hardening row. Both are defensive branches that handle corrupted persisted state: loadEntities reads task and candidate JSON raw, so neither the taskStore write validation nor candidateStore's record validation applies on load. The code is correct, and QA verified at runtime that it fails closed in both cases. But no test pins either branch, and a mutant that fails open passes the whole suite.

1. delivery/policy.ts protectedCheckShortfall: the validateExecutionContract catch returns protected-checks-unapproved. Mutant: `return []` there. It survives, and a corrupt requiredChecks then reads as satisfied: checkOwed is true and no token is produced.
   Proposed test, in requiredChecks.delivery.test.ts:
   - `h.state.tasks.set('task-1', {...task(), executionContract: {requiredChecks: [{...defs[0], bogus: 1}, defs[1]]}})`
   - expect missing() == ['protected-checks-unapproved']
   - expect projection requiredCheckSatisfied false

2. protectedDrift: the duplicate-path guard (`candidate.has(path)`) returns null, which yields unmeasured. Mutant: drop the guard. It survives, and the last duplicate wins.
   Proposed test: a candidate with `[{path: e[0].path, oid: OID}, ...e]`, and again with the duplicate last. Expect ['protected-checks-unmeasured'] both times.

Both tests passed on the HEAD 8eec4a2 bytes (18/18) and killed their mutant, in a scratch copy only (/tmp/qa-v01-bin/extra-tests.ts.txt).

comments.author: worker-7d158765
comments.content:
Hand-forward from CQ-V02 (Candidate execution binding):
- CheckRun now carries an optional REPORTED `outcome` (passed | code-failure | infra-failure | timeout | skipped | inconclusive). policy.ts passedOn counts only `passed`, or an absent outcome at exit 0.
- state/deliveryProjection.ts checkFor still projects only {command, exitCode, source} into `latestCheckRun`, so an exit-0 infra-failure/timeout/skipped/inconclusive run looks like a pass in the IDE board.
- Display only: gating is fail-closed through the shared predicate. No reporter sends outcome yet; the wrappers' payloads are identity-less.
- V02 left projection/client exposure out of scope by plan. Consider adding `outcome` to latestCheckRun (and the JetBrains/VS Code renderers) when a consumer starts sending it.

comments.content:

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
CQ-V04 split (2026-10-29, the human's choice): V04 keeps the daemon core, CQ-V04b (task-340a07b33a764c65b2486d16b30d7aef) is the local-runner check dispatch client, and CQ-V04c (task-c4e076cd306f4f84a4aa08bf2a4682b2) is the honest host-gate outcome. Both are now in this row's dependsOn. Two items are handed to you.

1. Docs debt, which V04 leaves for your sweep:
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: a row for the new settings.checkEnvironments. It is a project.json-only list of human-approved check environment ids (the exact CheckRun.environment values), like deliveryPolicy. Absent approves none; it is read live, so removing an id revokes the evidence recorded in it; UPDATE_SETTINGS refuses it as unknown.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md: in the deliveryPolicy and executionProfile rows, the verified-local required-check rule. Only an authenticated observation counts: outcome 'passed', the current approved revision, a dispatch naming that owed check, and a listed environment. Add the new token required-checks-undeclared.

V04 itself documents only the record_check_dispatch admission, in MCP_SERVER.md.

2. Activation gap, not owned by any task yet: nothing invokes the V04b client for each strong-profile candidate. The wrappers' strong completion path, after freeze_candidate, would call it instead of the host gate and wait for the observations. Own it here, or split it out, before claiming trusted dispatch end to end.

executionContract.intendedBehavior:
Close out the CQ-V epic.
1. The landed CQ-V contracts are documented exactly as they landed, across seven docs.
2. One fresh full regression across the daemon, the proxy and the wrapper harnesses is green, and the slices' acceptance fixtures (V11, V12a, V12b) and wrapper modes (V07, V08, V08b) pass unchanged.
3. One adversarial whole-epic review finds no gate bypass, or files the fix and blocks on it.
This task edits no production or test code.
acceptanceCriteria: DoD 1: deliveryBypass.acceptance.test.ts (CQ-V12a) and the V07/V08/V08b postflight modes pass unchanged in the fresh run. The review finds no forged, stale, missing-check, target-race or receipt-crash path past a gate, or V12 blocks on a filed fix.
DoD 2: dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts (CQ-V12b) passes unchanged, and the review confirms that every non-test readiness call site passes the consumer through the one shared predicate.
DoD 3: all seven docs match the landed code, and the completion summary reports the regression numbers and the adversarial review findings, each with an owner.
DoD 4: a fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0, with its output supplied to complete_task.
invariants: No file under packages/moe-daemon/src/__acceptance__ is edited by this task.
Legacy and observe behavior unchanged; pre-existing suites unchanged.
No .moe edits, no Git writes, no runner key material in any doc.
compatibility: Docs keep describing legacy/observe behavior as unchanged wherever it is unchanged.
Peer hunks in CONFIGURATION.md (bdf6db6f), MCP_SERVER.md/SCHEMA.md (C11a, bc8410af) and scripts/CLAUDE.md (c2a900aa) stay intact.

Code defects found by the review become new tasks (moe.create_task), never edits in this task.

The isolated Linux snapshot gate of mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate, as CQ-V02 and CQ-V09 used it for packages/moe-daemon/package.json npm test.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:

- V03a (server/runnerChannel.ts): RUNNER_KEY_HEADER x-moe-runner-key, ensureRunnerKey, authenticateRunner and runnerKeyPath. The key lives at <MOE_RUNNER_KEY_DIR|~/.moe/runner-keys>/<sha256(projectPath)[:32]>.key, mode 0600. runnerId is runner-<16 hex>. ToolCallContext.runner.
- V03b (state/checkObservationStore.ts): recordCheckDispatch, recordCheckObservation and isAuthenticatedCheckRun; records under .moe/checks/dispatches and .moe/checks/observations.
- V03: tools moe.record_check_dispatch and moe.record_check_observation, refusing with RUNNER_CHANNEL_REQUIRED.
- V05 (delivery/repairPolicy.ts): resolveRepairPolicy and decideRepair; settings.repairPolicy {maxCodeRepairs 3, maxInfraRetries 2, 0-10}.
- V06 (delivery/reviewBinding.ts): assertReviewedCandidateCurrent; qa_approve/qa_reject attemptId, generation, sessionId and candidateId. Refusals: STEP_ENTRY_IDENTITY_REQUIRED, ATTEMPT_SUPERSEDED, ATTEMPT_NOT_RUNNING, PLAN_REVISION_NOT_APPROVED, CONTEXT_RECEIPT_STALE, REVIEWED_CANDIDATE_REQUIRED, CANDIDATE_MISMATCH.

- V07: PINNED_ATTEMPT_PROFILE; MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_INTENT_INCOMPLETE and _UNWRITABLE.
- V08: MOE_COMMIT_REFUSED_UNRECONCILED_INTENT, MOE_FINALIZE_DEFERRED_RECEIPT and MOE_DELIVERY_PROOF_NOT_TRANSFERRED.
- V09: dependencyShortfall and isDependencySatisfied gain a consumer; tokens legacy-delivery, prerequisite-missing and archived-without-verified-delivery.
- V10: the check-architecture command (runCheckArchitecture; --rules, --base, --tree; exit 0, 1 or 2).

- V12b: dependencyProjection.acceptance.test.ts and latestCheckRun.outcome.
V04 and V05b were unplanned when this plan was written; read their landed diffs.

JetBrains reads the delivery projection with Gson, which ignores unknown keys, so additive projection keys are wire-safe.
